reason: This passage (Exodus 14) depicts Yahweh as explicitly protective and supportive of the Hebrew people. Yahweh fights for them against the pursuing Egyptians (יְהוָה יִלָּחֵם לָכֶם—'Yahweh will fight for you'), provides supernatural protection through the pillar of cloud and fire, enables their safe passage across the Red Sea, and destroys their enemies. The text culminates with the statement that 'Yahweh saved (ויושע) Israel... from the hand of Egypt' and describes the Israelites' fearful reverence and belief in response. These are acts of deliverance and covenant faithfulness, the opposite of antagonism.
